thread:
carla (Support): raising an escalation — ACME reports p95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~480ms around 13:12 UTC after the CUDA/driver rollout. They also see intermittent 5xx auth failures when requests hit node pool A. full ticket: INC-4521 :flag-us:

james (Customer Success): customer is getting paged, says impact on search product. sent repro prompt + example request ids.

dave (eng-infra): noted — we rolled driver v520.61 -> v525.12 to eu-west-1 at 12:50. autoscaler bumped a bunch of hosts into the new pool. checking kernel and nvme metrics now.

bob (eng-runtime): looking at ingress traces — majority of slow tails correlate with nodes that have i/o sched higher iowait and KV cache misses. p95 spike graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc/p95-overview?from=now-2h

alice (eng-sre): any auth error logs? could be token refresh failures if time skewed after restart.

carla (Support): customer sent an example error: `{"error":"auth token refresh failed","code":401}` for some requests, but most are just slow responses (200s eventually).

infra-bot: host-alert eu-west-1-gpu-07: nvme_io_wait > 200ms (12:55 UTC), kernel dmesg includes: `nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, resetting controller` repeated.

dave (eng-infra): that nvme reset pattern matches the hosts that got driver + firmware update. I also see `firmware update applied` in node bootstrap logs for those hosts. suspicious for storage path regressions.

bob (eng-runtime): reproducer: run load test with large embed model, sequence len ~1024, concurrency 30 on driver-updated hosts. CLI: ```ab -n 1000 -c 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" https://api.redwood/v1/generate``` Observed p95 ~420ms vs baseline ~110ms. KV cache hit rate dropped ~35%.

alice (eng-sre): mitigation options: 1) drain traffic from updated pool -> route to legacy driver pool, 2) roll back driver/firmware on a small canary, 3) apply host-level i/o qdisc tweaks to deprioritize background flushes. Which is fastest?

james (Customer Success): customer wants traffic routed away first if possible. they cannot accept degraded SLAs.

dave (eng-infra): I can add a routing rule to exclude pool eu-west-1-driver525, prep a canary rollback, and also throttle background scrub tasks. doing route change now.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift job started: route 80% -> legacy-pool, 20% -> updated-pool (gradual 10% steps). job id: rs-789.

bob (eng-runtime): after shifting 80% we see p95 drop to ~150ms on customer traces for new requests within 5m. KV cache hit rate for customer restored. Auth 401s reduced to baseline.

carla (Support): relaying to ACME — they confirm reduced error rate and better p95 on new requests, but still seeing occasional tails on sessions routed to updated pool. :thumbsup:

alice (eng-sre): plan: keep majority traffic off updated pool, escalate to infra for root cause. we should reproduce on isolated lab host with same driver+firmware and run low-level fio + nvme stress and also reproduce token refresh pattern. dave, can you provide affected host IDs and firmware versions?

dave (eng-infra): affected hosts: eu-west-1-gpu-07/09/12, driver 525.12, firmware 2.3.7. I'll spin up a lab host with identical stack and run fio +driver stress. also collecting `dmesg`, `nvme-cli list`, `iostat -x 1 20`.

bob (eng-runtime): adding test plan and repro steps to the incident doc: ```- provision lab host with driver 525.12 + fw 2.3.7
- deploy inference runtime + synthetic load generator
- run 30 concurrent sequence=1024 requests for 15m while collecting iostat/dmesg
- compare KV cache metrics and token refresh logs```

carla (Support): keeping customer updated. will offer a credit if degradation persists.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift job rs-789 completed: 90% -> legacy-pool, 10% -> updated-pool.

bob (eng-runtime): follow-up: when we reproduced in lab, heavy nvme reset events correlated with driver+firmware combination and a particular kernel path that serializes io under specific queue-depth patterns — root cause likely storage driver interaction. token refresh 401s were secondary caused by timeouts and retry storms when requests hit those nodes.

alice (eng-sre): next steps: 1) block full rollout of driver 525.12 cluster-wide, 2) work with vendor on firmware/driver interaction, 3) schedule rollback for remaining hosts, 4) add auto-fallback routing if host nvme_io_wait > threshold. I'll open a follow-up RFC for fallback policy.

dave (eng-infra): rolling rollback plan for remaining updated hosts queued, ETA 2h. posting playbook to incident doc.

carla (Support): thanks all — keeping ACME notified. closing this thread when rollback completes and customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
